before.rationale: Ahab reports Elijah's killing of the prophets with the sword; the preceding account narrates his seizure and slaughter of Baal's prophets at the Kishon wadi. The report recalls that particular action.

after.rationale: Ahab reports Elijah's killing of the prophets with the sword; the preceding account narrates the people's seizure of Baal's prophets at Elijah's order and Elijah bringing them down to the Kishon wadi and slaughtering them. The report recalls that particular action while retaining the distinct agents.

changes.reason: Distinguish the people who seize the prophets at Elijah order from Elijah who brings them to Kishon and slaughters them.

before.rationale: The son of Ader drinks himself drunk at noon with thirty-two allied kings; the earlier siegework command was issued while he and his kings drank in tents. The repeated setting marks the condition of the opposing leadership.

after.rationale: The son of Ader drinks himself drunk at noon with thirty-two allied kings; the earlier siegework command was issued while he and his kings drank in tents. The repeated setting marks the condition of the opposing leadership.

changes.reason: Earlier target says drinking, while source explicitly says drunk; use the common drinking term in the category.

before.rationale: Ahab leaves the prophetic encounter confounded and dispirited for Samaria; after Naboth's refusal his spirit had likewise become troubled. The literary parallel compares his narrated distress after opposed desires, while retaining the distinct circumstances.

after.rationale: Ahab leaves the prophetic encounter confounded and dispirited for Samaria; after Naboth's refusal his spirit had likewise become troubled. The literary parallel compares his explicitly stated distress in the different settings of the prophetic rebuke and Naboth's refusal, without assigning an additional motive.

changes.reason: Remove an additional opposed-desire motive and compare the actual stated distress in the two settings.

before.rationale: Israel's king announces his own concealment and tells Jehoshaphat to put on my clothing, then enters concealed. Chronicles repeats both actions with cover wording. The source's my clothing is preserved rather than changed to a generic command to wear royal robes.

after.rationale: Israel's king announces his own concealment and tells Jehoshaphat to put on my clothing, then enters concealed. Chronicles repeats the concealment and clothing directive, using cover wording. The source's my clothing is preserved rather than changed to a generic command to wear royal robes.

changes.reason: Distinguish concealment performed by Israel king from the clothing directive to Jehoshaphat; do not imply his compliance was independently narrated.

before.relationship: Local royal death and succession notice
before.rationale: The herald's continued announcement states that the king is dead and narrates burial in Samaria; the regnal notice then says Ahab slept with his fathers and Ahaziah reigned in his place. The latter names the succession following the narrated death.

after.relationship: Local royal death and succession notice
after.rationale: The continued herald announcement states that the king is dead; the narrator then reports burial in Samaria. The regnal notice says Ahab slept with his fathers and Ahaziah reigned in his place. The latter names the succession following the narrated death.

changes.reason: Attribute the king-is-dead announcement to the herald and the following burial report to the narrator.

before.relationship: Repeated royal accession notice with unresolved synchronism
before.rationale: Both notices place Jehoshaphat son of Asa over Judah, but this one dates his accession to Ahab's fourth year and the earlier continuation to Omri's eleventh. The shared named accession is retained as a partial connection; the different synchronisms remain unresolved and receive no chronology-reconciliation credit.

after.relationship: Repeated royal accession notice with unresolved synchronism

The shared named accession is retained as a partial connection; the different synchronisms remain unresolved and receive no chronology-reconciliation credit.

changes.reason: The target names accession but does not separately say Judah; retain the shared named accession without expanding its wording or solving different dates.
